raw_plan.interpretation: One English acquisition email for an agency or freelance developer considering a repeatable analytics option for client sites. Because the relationship is unknown and recipient qualification is unverified, the email will address the audience-level decision and invite inspection of the documented data design before signup or deployment.

intent.desired_action: Inspect the documented data scope and decide whether Simple Analytics is worth evaluating for a client site.

raw_plan.reader: An agency or freelance developer assessing privacy-friendly analytics options for client websites and wanting a technical basis they can explain to clients.
raw_plan.reader_segment: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites
raw_plan.reader_scope: Agencies and freelance developers evaluating a cookie-free analytics default for suitable client builds. Do not imply that every recipient currently uses GA4, manages multiple live sites, or has already encountered a consent or DPA dispute.
raw_plan.promise: Simple Analytics gives developers a concrete, inspectable analytics data model they can assess for client sites without relying on a generic privacy-friendly label.
raw_plan.orientation: Simple Analytics is a cookie-free website analytics option that agencies and freelance developers can evaluate as a repeatable default across suitable client sites.
raw_plan.arc: In this single email, move the reader from skepticism about privacy-friendly analytics claims to interest in Simple Analytics because its collection and storage choices are documented and can be inspected before adoption.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: The single slot leads with the strongest supported fit for this solution-aware audience: the concrete data design behind the privacy proposition. The public documentation is a lower-friction next step than registration because it lets the reader assess the relevant fields and boundaries before deciding whether installation is worthwhile. A self-guided installation evaluation is retained as a complete alternative proposition, but it asks for more commitment and does not answer the reader's first technical eligibility question as directly. No customer outcome or blanket legal exemption is needed to make the primary case. A readable copy of the currently unavailable homepage source, or verification of its missing details, would most change this campaign.

emails.selection_reason: The audience research shows direct skepticism about whether privacy-friendly analytics claims reflect the actual collection mechanism. Simple Analytics can answer that question with documented technical specifics that are relevant when recommending an analytics stack to clients.

value_case.reader_benefit: For suitable client sites, the developer can provide website-traffic analytics with a data footprint that is concrete enough to review and explain: no cookies, no stored IP addresses, and a documented set of processed website and device fields that are not linked to identifiable users.
value_case.mechanism: Simple Analytics operates without cookies, discards IP addresses immediately rather than storing them, and documents processing Page URL, Referrer, UTM parameters, Time zone, and Device and browser type without linking those metrics to identifiable users.
decision_conditions: These facts describe Simple Analytics' documented technical behavior; they do not establish a universal legal conclusion for every client configuration or jurisdiction.
Suitability still needs to be checked against each client's requirements.

claim_conditions: Frame the application to client sites conditionally because no recipient or company has been qualified.
Keep legal applicability separate from the documented collection and storage design.
emails.target_audience: Agency or freelance developer choosing the analytics stack for client sites
emails.job: Give the reader a concrete technical reason to consider Simple Analytics and get them to inspect its documented data scope before deciding whether to evaluate it on a client site.
emails.single_idea: Simple Analytics is worth considering as a client-site analytics default because its privacy proposition rests on inspectable collection choices: no cookies, no stored IP addresses, and a limited documented data scope that is not linked to identifiable users.
emails.felt_need: When choosing analytics for a client site, a privacy-friendly label is not enough; the underlying collection method has to withstand scrutiny.
emails.status_quo: Developers compare named analytics alternatives and debate whether their privacy and consent claims match the technical design.
emails.why_it_fails: A category label does not show which identifiers or fields are collected and stored, so it cannot settle whether the design fits a client's requirements.
emails.mechanism: Simple Analytics documents that it uses no cookies, discards IP addresses immediately, and processes a defined set of website and device fields without linking them to identifiable users.

alternative_arguments.selection_reason: A developer considering a repeatable default may instead respond to a practical way to explore the product and see installation guidance for a representative site.

value_case.reader_benefit: The developer can explore Simple Analytics on a representative site and see installation guidance selected for that site's detected technology before considering broader use across client builds.
value_case.mechanism: The onboarding flow scans the website and provides technology-dependent HTML code or another documented platform or framework installation option; the self-serve trial provides 14 days to explore Simple Analytics independently.
decision_conditions: Installation is performed per site and exact code placement can depend on the website.
The self-guided trial is distinct from the assisted 30-day GA4 proof of concept.

claim_conditions: Present this as an evaluation on a representative site, not proof of compatibility or economics across an entire client portfolio.

alternative_arguments.mechanism: After a website is added, Simple Analytics scans it and offers technology-dependent install code or another documented platform or framework option; the 14-day trial is self-guided.
alternative_arguments.belief_shift: Before: evaluating another analytics option may appear to require committing to a generic installation path. After: one representative site can be explored through a self-guided trial with technology-dependent installation guidance.
must_not_say: Do not promise one universal installation step or instant setup.
Do not claim compatibility with every client platform or framework.

Do not claim that testing one site proves suitability, cost, or scalability across a client portfolio.
alternative_arguments.objection: Will the installation path fit the kind of site I would use it on?
alternative_arguments.call_to_action: Start the 14-day self-guided trial on a representative site.
alternative_arguments.next_step_decision: Decide whether the installation flow and product are suitable for a practical evaluation on that type of client build.
alternative_arguments.next_step_value: The signup path provides access to the self-guided trial, where the reader can explore Simple Analytics and use the technology-dependent onboarding flow for a chosen website.
alternative_arguments.next_step_limit: One trial installation does not establish compatibility, commercial fit, or rollout effort across every client site.

events.preview_text: See the fields Simple Analytics processes before evaluating it for a client site.
events.body:
Before evaluating analytics for a client site, you can review the exact data footprint the service is designed to use.

Simple Analytics is cookie-free website analytics. It uses no persistent identifiers, stores no IP addresses—they are discarded immediately—and does not link its metrics to identifiable users.

Its public data-processing page lists the scope: Page URL, referrer, UTM parameters, time zone, and device and browser type. You can inspect these fields without signing up or installing anything.

This gives you a concrete model to review and explain, rather than a general privacy claim. Compare the documented fields with each client’s requirements, then decide whether Simple Analytics is suitable for an evaluation on their site.
